issues.description: extract_arch_from_url silently returns None, producing a malformed URL with literal 'None' in the path
issues.detail: When the regex misses, the function returns None and the caller interpolates it into '.../latest/None/Packages/...' via f-string. No exception, no log, just a broken lockfile downstream. Either raise loudly or skip with an error. Don't let a missing fact become a string-shaped fact.

issues.description: nevra[0] uses the filename's first character rather than parsing the package name's first letter
issues.detail: Koji's Packages layout uses the first letter of the package NAME. Using nevra[0].lower() conflates filename-first-char with name-first-letter; it works by accident today for packages like 389-ds-base, but the invariant is unstated and unenforced. Parse the NEVRA properly and assert the relationship.

issues.description: Race with coreos-koji-tagger acknowledged in commit message but unmitigated and undocumented in code
issues.detail: The fabricated URL is only valid after koji-tagger processes the merge commit. This temporal assumption lives only in the PR description, not in the code. Add a comment naming the assumption so the next person debugging a 404 finds it in seconds, and consider a retry/verify step.

issues.description: Arch should be read from the NEVRA filename suffix, not regex-scanned across the whole URL
issues.detail: Every RPM filename ends in .<arch>.rpm — the canonical value. Regex-searching the whole URL path for arch tokens creates two sources of truth that can disagree (e.g. /ppc64le-mirror/.../foo.x86_64.rpm would mis-classify). Read the arch from the filename, the actual fact.

issues.description: Hardcoded arch list and koji base URL should be module-level constants, not buried in function bodies
issues.detail: The supported arch set and koji path layout are load-bearing facts duplicated across functions. Hoist to module-level constants (SUPPORTED_ARCHES, koji_url_base). One edit instead of a grep when koji's layout changes. Small change, big readability win for the next maintainer.

issues.description: No unit tests for the new URL-rewriting functions despite easy local testability
issues.detail: use_koji_url_only and extract_arch_from_url are pure, deterministic, and trivially testable with a handful of representative URLs. A 15-20 line test would have caught both the nevra[0] and None-arch defects above. The author's claim that 'rpms.lock.yaml cannot be tested locally' does not apply to these pure helpers.

synthesis.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The panel agrees the approach — synthesizing koji URLs to work around DNF5's broken baseurl for secondary arches — is reasonable, but execution has two concrete defects all three reviewers flagged: extract_arch_from_url silently returns None and lets the literal string 'None' propagate into a malformed URL, and the Packages subdirectory uses nevra[0] (filename first char) rather than the package name's first letter (works by accident today). The race with coreos-koji-tagger is documented in the commit message and shipped unmitigated in code. Hoist constants, add unit tests for the pure helpers, and either fail loudly on arch-miss or read the arch from the NEVRA filename suffix where it actually lives.
